title: Forgiving input normalization
summary: Accept harmless formatting variations and normalize them when the meaning is unambiguous instead of forcing users to match machine formatting.
problem: Rigid formatting rules create avoidable validation errors for spaces, punctuation, casing, or common human formats.
use_when: Equivalent user formats can be safely normalized
The system can distinguish harmless formatting from ambiguous or incorrect data
avoid_when: The exact entered representation has legal, cryptographic, or audit significance
rationale: Validation should protect data meaning, not formatting preferences.
Accepting benign variation prevents unnecessary error-recovery loops.

prefer_alternatives_if: Exact formatting is itself meaningful or required
use_if: Equivalent user formats can be safely normalized
The system can distinguish harmless formatting from ambiguous or incorrect data

requirements: Explain true format constraints before submission when they matter.
Do not require users to visually detect invisible formatting characters.
Trim or ignore harmless formatting where safe.
Reject ambiguity, not harmless presentation differences.
Normalize after capture rather than forcing exact keystrokes.
